title: fix: batch quest reward inserts safely
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Sends each pending reward as its own prepared insert inside one transactional D1 batch.
- Removes the schema-sensitive multi-row chunk size that exceeded D1's 100-bound-parameter limit.
- Preserves idempotency and returns only IDs for rows that were actually inserted.
- Adds coverage for a 12-reward scan, matching the production failure.

Validation:
- `npx biome check --write ../shared/billing/rewards.ts test/integration/rewards.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
- Vitest Workers pool currently exits before loading any test file, including an unrelated existing test.

gist.headline: Rewards, one seed at a time
gist.blurb: The quest reward garden no longer trips over a crowded wheelbarrow. Larger batches now settle safely, with every earned Pollen seed landing where it should.
gist.summary: Quest reward processing now sends each pending reward as an individual prepared insert within one transactional D1 batch, avoiding D1's 100-bound-parameter limit while preserving idempotency and inserted-ID reporting.
gist.impact: Users completing larger Quest reward batches can reliably receive their earned Pollen, including scans with 12 pending rewards that previously hit the database parameter limit.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden keeper using a tiny tool belt to place individual glowing Pollen seeds into separate pots on a conveyor feeding a cozy retro database terminal. A friendly CRT monitor robot counts twelve successful seed pots while code-plants and flowers grow around the terminal, representing transactional, idempotent reward inserts without an overloaded batch.
